thread:
PagerBot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] decode-stream pool 'decode-stream-prod' reporting repeated CUDA OOMs across 3 alloc nodes. Auto-quarantine applied to offending nodes. Incident INC-2026-052 created. root_ts=4415556666

Eva L.: joining bridge — grabbing logs and current routing. @Sanjay P. can you validate if any recent deploy touched decode kernels?

Sanjay P.: not from me, last kernel pin was ~12h ago. I see a sudden spike in long-running streaming sessions from a single client id (client=acme-sales). Possible runaway generation. Pulling traces.

Maria K.: oncall handoff note: Ash T. was night oncall, handed to me at 07:10 but I forwarded bridge to Eva for decode expertise. tagging @Ops Bot for autoscaling telemetry.

Ops Bot: autoscaler: attempted scale +2 gpus -> failed due to container crash loop on new nodes (OOM during image startup). Reverting additions.

Eva L.: quick customer-impact check: request drops metric for streaming decode went from baseline 0.2% -> 9.8% in last 12m. Error samples show CUDA OOM and "out of memory during backward/kv cache" even during generation. Most correlated with messages having no max_tokens header (client not setting).

Sanjay P.: logs snippet: ```
E [decode.cc:245] CUDA out of memory while allocating activation buffer (size=540MB)
W [streaming] client=acme-sales session=xyz elapsed=00:05:31 tokens_generated=4800
```

Eva L.: immediate mitigation plan (short list):
1) Enable server-side per-request token cap (force max_tokens=1024) for decode-stream-prod traffic.
2) Route heavy clients (client=acme-sales) to a smaller model variant (redwood/small-1.2b-quant) with degraded latency but safe memory footprint.
3) Quarantine offending nodes, drain active sessions slowly (no hard restart) to avoid mass drops.
4) Notify affected CSMs and post status page update.

Ash T.: doing the token cap now. Command: ```
redwoodctl routes update --env prod --route decode-stream --set header.x-max-tokens=1024 --selector "region=us-west"
``` Applying to global route in 30s.

Ops Bot: route update applied by Ash T. -> confirmation id rt-9876. Telemetry will report effect in ~1m.

Sanjay P.: enabling fallback routing for client=acme-sales: ```
redwoodctl policy add-fallback --route decode-stream --selector client_id=acme-sales --fallback redwood/small-1.2b-quant --prioritize cost-safe
```
Fallback policy in place.

Maria K.: note: we should also enforce a header check at the edge to reject requests without client-supplied max_tokens above 4096 next deploy, but that's medium-term. For now throttling + fallback.

Eva L.: customer impact: flagged 3 customers with >5% error rate: acme-sales (12.3%), finlytics (6.1%), internal-prod-test (7.8%). Drafting account ping for acme-sales. Someone from AMs to send triage note? @Maria K.

Maria K.: I'll coordinate with AMs. Short message to accounts: "We experienced streaming generation instability leading to degraded responses; temporary routing and token caps applied; engineering investigating root cause; we'll follow up with ETA for full resolution."

Sanjay P.: after fallback and token cap, OOMs dropped sharply on quarantined nodes, but we still see occasional container crash at startup when trying to spin new decode workers. Suspect a kernel memory regression in recent runtime build 2.14.7.

Eva L.: can we roll back runtime to 2.14.5 on decode nodes only? If rollout system supports canary to 10% first.

Ash T.: I can trigger rollback to 2.14.5 on a canary subset. Command: ```
redwood-deploy --env prod --group decode-canary --image runtime:2.14.5 --max-inflight 10
``` I'll kick that off after spike settles.

Ops Bot: telemetry: after token cap + fallback, request drops down to 0.9% within 2m. Streaming latency slightly higher for fallback clients (~+120ms). Quarantined nodes showing OOM count 0 after drain.

PagerBot: incident severity escalated to Sev2 due to customer impact and partial outage risk. Pager duty: notify oncall escalation policy.

Eva L.: coordinating post-mit steps:
- Keep nodes quarantined and maintain fallback routing for 1h.
- Rollback runtime on canary group and monitor OOMs for 30m.
- If canary stable, roll forward rollback to remaining decode nodes in waves.
- Post-customer follow-up and RCA draft.

Sanjay P.: collecting traces for root cause: correlation looks like long-lived sessions without client-side truncation + kv cache growth + an allocation regression in 2.14.7 decode allocator. Will upload trace bundle to /artifacts/incidents/INC-2026-052/trace.tar.gz

Maria K.: prepping status page entry and account emails. ETA for next update 20m.

Eva L.: current status: mitigations applied (server token cap, fallback routing, node quarantine). Request drops reduced to 0.9%. Rolling canary rollback queued. Bridge remains open.

Ash T.: canary rollback started at 4415556980, canary group 10 nodes. Monitoring.

Ops Bot: canary telemetry: 10m after rollback, canary group OOM count=0, drop rate for canary clients=0.15%

Eva L.: if canary stays green for 30m we will expand rollback. If anything spikes we revert to throttles + fallback.

PagerBot: logging incident actions to INC-2026-052. Assigning RCA owners: S.P. (root cause) and E.L. (mitigation/comm).

Maria K.: noted. I'll send AM notes now and update status page.

Eva L.: thanks team — will keep thread updated with progress and final timeline for full rollout. :white_check_mark:
